correctness.rationale: For same-forcing states the differences satisfy u'=-A(u+v), v'=-B(u'+v) with 0<=A<=a<1 and 0<=B<=b<1. The hexagonal norm max(|u|,|v|,|u+v|) contracts by q=a+b-ab<1. Pullback limits give a unique bounded bilateral response, and perturbations yield the quantitative global bound (a||e_p||+b||e_n||)/(1-q). Tanh responses meet every domain condition and attain q at the differential level; the gain-one affine model gives genuine 2-cycles. Exact-rational and nonlinear checks in verify.py passed but are not substitutes for the proof.

value.rationale: The initiating neuromorphic event-feedback theorem has only the conservative gain-sum criterion for general fading memory. This sharp, sign-sensitive criterion gives robust unique rhythms with both gains as high as 4/5 (summed gain 8/5), quantifies full-trajectory convergence and response sensitivity, and identifies an exact failure boundary. The sharp inequality relies on the event chronology and its inhibitory sign, making it a structural, experimentally relevant extension rather than a parameter substitution. The general nonlinear forced theorem is not inferred from linear tests.
